recent_posts.title: Interactive Live Streaming for In-Person Events
recent_posts.summary: A developer relations professional shares how her team created a 10-hour live stream for their company conference, engaging 18,000 remote viewers for just $15,000 instead of spending $230,000 on traditional hybrid event infrastructure. The approach involved two hosts, 55 guests across 42 segments, interactive games with prizes, and strategic use of StreamYard. Key lessons include managing host rotation to prevent burnout, building guest rapport through documentation rather than pre-meetings, and creating connection between in-person and virtual audiences through conversational interviews and community engagement.

recent_posts.title: Community in the Age of AI
recent_posts.summary: A developer relations leader at HubSpot shares their strategy for integrating AI into developer community management while preserving human connection. The approach focuses on using AI to automate repetitive support questions through a bot called Sprocky, freeing up time for meaningful peer-to-peer interactions, mentorship programs, and events. The strategy includes measuring success through peer connections rather than volume metrics, creating AI-focused mentorship tracks, and building partnerships with AI agents. The goal is to help developers get unblocked faster on simple questions while fostering deeper relationships and career growth within the community.

recent_posts.title: Activating the DevRel Flywheel to Create Lasting Results
recent_posts.summary: Workshop transcript covering the flywheel methodology for developer relations teams. Explains how to build a DevRel flywheel by defining goals aligned with organizational objectives, mapping activities and metrics to growth stages (acquisition, adoption, advocacy), identifying friction points in processes, and creating prioritized action plans. Includes practical exercises using a spreadsheet template to inventory tasks, assess team workload, and prioritize initiatives based on impact versus effort.

recent_posts.title: Framework for building effective video content in product led growth
recent_posts.summary: A framework for creating effective video content in product-led growth strategies. Covers the three-stage production process (pre-production, production, post-production), the limbic-logic-action video structure, and five core laws: specificity, limbic priority, funnel alignment, outcome obsession, and trackable metrics. Emphasizes starting with 'why', focusing on outcomes over features, targeting specific personas, and measuring beyond vanity metrics like views. Includes practical homework assignments and a downloadable PLG video playbook.

recent_posts.title: Building a custom sticker vending machine
recent_posts.summary: A developer advocate shares how to build engaging physical demos for conferences, using a custom sticker vending machine as the primary example. The presentation covers the psychology of interactive demos, hardware components (servos, Raspberry Pi, motor controllers), prototyping with cardboard, and integrating web apps with robotics. Includes practical tips for transporting demos, debugging hardware at events, and making technical concepts tangible through hands-on experiences. Demonstrates how to use the Viam platform to control hardware with minimal code and discusses other demo ideas like robotic arms, computer vision applications, and automated systems.

recent_posts.title: DevRel without the developer
recent_posts.summary: LLMs and AI agents are fundamentally changing how developers discover and consume technical documentation. Instead of visiting docs directly, developers now ask AI tools for answers, making traditional DevRel metrics like page views less meaningful. To adapt, DevRel teams should optimize documentation for LLM consumption through self-contained sections, clear error messages, code snippets, and proper chunking. Key strategies include tracking brand mentions in LLM responses, implementing LLM-friendly formats like llm.txt files, adding AI-powered chatbots, and providing markdown export options. The core principle remains unchanged: helping developers succeed, just through different channels.

recent_posts.title: How gamification builds trust and scales developer communities
recent_posts.summary: Gamification in developer relations has evolved beyond simple tutorials and badges into a strategic framework for building trust and scaling developer communities. By connecting education, contribution tracking, and recognition systems into a cohesive journey, organizations can transform isolated engagement tactics into infrastructure that compounds trust over time. The key is designing systems that remember developer contributions, create visible progression paths, and reward meaningful participation—turning lurkers into leaders through automated recognition and interconnected programs that feed into each other rather than operating in silos.

recent_posts.title: YouTube-based DevRel
recent_posts.summary: A former Twilio developer evangelist shares lessons from growing a YouTube channel from zero to 8,500 subscribers in one year. The talk covers why YouTube is an effective DevRel platform compared to traditional tactics like conference travel and blog posts, especially as AI changes how developers find solutions. Key insights include the importance of packaging (titles and thumbnails), respecting viewer time through efficient content, managing the time-intensive production process, and overcoming psychological challenges of solo content creation. The speaker emphasizes that developers have an unfair advantage on YouTube due to the combination of coding skills, speaking ability, and basic video production knowledge being rare, with relatively low competition compared to other niches.

recent_posts.title: Building technical demos that ride trending topics for maximum developer engagement
recent_posts.summary: A developer advocate shares strategies for creating technical demos that capitalize on trending topics and viral moments. The approach involves building content around current events, product launches, pop culture, and holidays to maximize visibility and engagement. Key lessons include prioritizing timing over technical complexity, being prepared to build quickly, using humor and entertainment value, and targeting niche communities. Examples include ChatGPT over SMS, Wordle clones, and AI-powered apps tied to cultural moments. Success metrics focus on social media engagement, GitHub trends, and developer feedback rather than just view counts.

recent_posts.title: Docs, LLMs, agents - using AI to create a content feedback loop
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates how AI agents can automatically improve documentation by analyzing user interactions, support tickets, and code changes. The system uses three specialized agents: an insight finder that identifies documentation gaps, a content architect that determines where updates belong, and a smart publisher that creates pull requests. The approach transforms scattered knowledge from support conversations and code repositories into structured documentation updates, creating a continuous feedback loop that keeps docs current without manual intervention.
